comment: The MCP wire schema, frozen.  Read by test/cmacs/cmacs-wire-schema.el.

Each block is what tools/list returned for one tool while it was a hand-written C handler: name, description, inputSchema and annotations exactly as a client received them (annotations is absent when the C set no hint, which a client reads as not read-only).
`source' is the C file that registered it, `order' its position in that file, `ifdef' the configure flags the registration was compiled under.  A client never saw those three.

This file is edited on purpose and never regenerated wholesale.  Changing a published tool's parameters means editing its block in the same commit.  A new tool is added with cmacs-wire-schema-freeze-registry-tool, or by hand, when it should be held to its schema; tools sorted by name.

tools.name: ai_call
tools.description: Send PROMPT to an AI provider and return the final answer (synchronous).  Like ai_prompt, but with 'tools':true the model is given the built-in agent tools (bash/read/write/edit/glob/grep/ls/web_fetch) and runs a multi-turn tool loop.  WARNING: a tool loop blocks the cmacs main thread for its whole duration.  Optional 'provider' / 'system' / 'model' behave as for ai_prompt.
Give the model the built-in agent tools

tools.name: ai_embed_similarity
tools.description: Cosine similarity of two texts' embeddings, in [-1, 1]: 1 is the same direction, 0 unrelated, -1 opposite.  Use it to judge whether two passages mean the same thing -- near-duplicate detection, or checking an answer against a source.  Needs a local embedding provider (ollama).  Optional 'model' overrides the default embedding model.  To SEARCH the notes corpus use memory_search instead; this compares two specific strings.

tools.name: ai_list_models
tools.description: List the model names each cmacs-ai provider offers, as a JSON object mapping provider to an array of models.  Optional 'provider' restricts the query to one provider; otherwise all providers are queried (unavailable ones report inline).

tools.name: ai_list_providers
tools.description: Return the list of supported cmacs-ai provider symbols.

tools.name: ai_lql
tools.description: Run an LQL query on the libresearch server and return its rows (at most 100 shown).  LQL pipes search results: search "glib", category: CODE | filter extra.stars > 100 | fields title, url -- or the shorthand gtk docs | filter site("docs.gtk.org").  'explain' returns the plan without running it.  An invalid query reports the server's position and caret excerpt.

tools.name: ai_open_chat
tools.description: Open a cmacs-ai chat buffer.  If PROMPT is given, the prompt is sent as the first user turn and streamed.  Optional 'model' overrides the provider's default model.  Returns the buffer name.

tools.name: ai_prompt
tools.description: Send PROMPT to an AI provider via cmacs-ai (synchronous).  Optional 'provider' (claude / openai / gemini / grok / ollama / claude-code / opencode / claude-tmux / grok-build / antigravity / cursor) overrides the default; optional 'system' is a system prompt; optional 'model' overrides the provider's default model.

tools.name: ai_research
tools.description: Research a question on the web with libresearch and return a cited answer: the answer with numbered citations [n], then the sources (title, URL).  Needs a libresearch server (cmacs-ai-libresearch-url). 'deep' lets the server run follow-up searches; 'pages' (1-20) is how many pages it reads.  WARNING: a run takes minutes, and the cmacs Lisp thread waits for it (the network runs on a worker thread).

tools.name: ai_web_fetch
tools.description: Read a web page's text through libresearch (the server applies its own SSRF guard).  'archive' is never (default), fallback (use the Wayback Machine when the live page fails) or only; 'max_chars' (100-1000000) caps the text.  Returns title, URL, the archived copy if one stood in, then the text.

tools.name: apropos
tools.description: Search for Emacs symbols matching a pattern. Returns one symbol per line.

pattern.description: Regexp pattern to match against symbol names

tools.name: backtrace
tools.description: Get the current Lisp backtrace.

tools.name: bacon_eval
tools.description: Run a command in the embedded bacon shell. Returns the exit code and captured stdout/stderr.

tools.name: cad_assembly_bom
tools.description: Assembly NAME's bill of materials (part, quantity, volume, mass).

tools.name: cad_assembly_info
tools.description: Assembly NAME's solved state, DOF, and per-instance transforms.

tools.name: cad_assembly_interference
tools.description: Interferences (overlapping instance pairs + volume) in assembly NAME.

tools.name: cad_assembly_set_joint
tools.description: Drive JOINT (id) of assembly NAME to VALUE and re-solve (no source re-eval); report the new instance transforms.

tools.name: cad_eval
tools.description: Re-evaluate a part; report ok+parts/error.

tools.name: cad_export
tools.description: Export the part to OUT in FORMAT (stl/stl-ascii/obj/step/iges).

tools.name: cad_feature_tree
tools.description: The part's feature (CSG) tree as indented text.

tools.name: cad_get_source
tools.description: Return a part's source text.

tools.name: cad_inspect
tools.description: Mass properties: volume, area, triangles, watertight, COM, bbox.

tools.name: cad_open
tools.description: Open a .cad/.ccad part; returns its language + capabilities.

tools.name: cad_params
tools.description: List a part's parameters and ranges.

tools.name: cad_patch_source
tools.description: Replace the single occurrence of OLD with NEW in a part, then re-evaluate. Token-economical edits; errors if OLD is absent/ambiguous.

tools.name: cad_print
tools.description: Upload GCODE to PRINTER. A print only STARTS when BOTH start and confirm are true; otherwise it only uploads (the safe default).

tools.name: cad_printers
tools.description: List configured printers.

tools.name: cad_section
tools.description: Section the part by an X/Y/Z plane at OFFSET; report segments + perimeter.

tools.name: cad_set_source
tools.description: Replace a part's whole SOURCE, write it, re-evaluate, and report ok+parts or the error with its source location. The edit-eval loop.

tools.name: cad_slice
tools.description: Export the part to STL and slice it to G-code (waits, default 300s).

tools.name: cad_snapshot
tools.description: Render the part in a workbench viewport and return an inline PNG.

tools.name: calc_convert_units
tools.description: Evaluate EXPRESSION and convert it to UNITS; with no UNITS, reduce it to base SI.  Knows CODATA physical constants (c, G, h, hbar, k, Nav, me, mp), so '2 * G * 1.989e30 kg / c^2' reduces to the Schwarzschild radius of the Sun in metres, and '60 mph' converts to 'm/s'.

units.description: Target units, e.g. m/s; omit to reduce to base SI

tools.name: calc_describe
tools.description: Describe one calculator by NAME: its title, category, arguments, return value and documentation.

tools.name: calc_eval
tools.description: Evaluate a calculator EXPRESSION numerically and return the result.  Uses desktop-calculator semantics: '/' and '*' associate left to right (so 2/3*4 is 2.667), angles are radians, and symbolic constants fold (e^(i*pi) is -1).  Arbitrary precision.  All registered calculators are callable as functions, e.g. 'bscall(100,100,0.05,0.2,1)' or 'lorentz(0.9)'.  Bad input is reported as an error rather than echoed back unevaluated.

tools.name: calc_eval_symbolic
tools.description: Evaluate a calculator EXPRESSION symbolically, permitting free variables.  This is the computer-algebra path: deriv(x^3,x), integ(x^2,x), solve(x^2-4=0,x), taylor(sin(x),x,5), factor, expand.  Use calc_eval instead when a number is wanted.

tools.name: calc_list
tools.description: List the registered calculators, optionally only those in one CATEGORY (financial, physics, relativity, tax, ...).  Each is callable as a function from calc_eval.

tools.name: cmacs.c.addr_to_source
tools.description: Resolve a runtime address ADDR to (file line function).

tools.name: cmacs.c.call_handle
tools.description: Call a JIT compilation HANDLE with ARGS.  Phase 2 stub.

tools.name: cmacs.c.compile_snippet
tools.description: Compile a C SOURCE string to a callable handle.  Phase 2 --- currently returns the cmacs-cintrospect-not-implemented sentinel.

tools.name: cmacs.c.defun_info
tools.description: Return a plist describing the DEFUN named SYMBOL (Lisp side).

tools.name: cmacs.c.function_source
tools.description: Return (file . line) for the C function NAME, or nil.

tools.name: cmacs.c.list
tools.description: List C-level entities of KIND (symbol|defun|object), optionally filtered by GLOB.  Returns a list of plists.

tools.name: cmacs.c.patch_defun
tools.description: Hot-patch the DEFUN named SYMBOL to call the function at ADDR.  Gated on `cmacs-mcp-cintrospect-enable-patching' (default nil).

tools.name: cmacs.c.patch_log
tools.description: List currently-applied patches.

tools.name: cmacs.c.stack_trace
tools.description: Return a list of frame plists describing the current C stack.

tools.name: cmacs.c.symbol_info
tools.description: Return a plist describing the C symbol named NAME (file, line, addr, kind, object, size).

tools.name: cmacs.c.type_info
tools.description: Return a plist describing the C type NAME (struct/union/enum) with field offsets, sizes, and types.

tools.name: cmacs.c.unpatch_all
tools.description: Panic button --- restore every patched DEFUN.  Returns the count.  NOT gated by enable-patching defcustom (you always want a panic out).

tools.name: cmacs.c.unpatch_defun
tools.description: Restore the original C function for the DEFUN named SYMBOL.

tools.name: completions
tools.description: Get completion candidates for a symbol name prefix. Returns up to 100 matches.

tools.name: create_buffer
tools.description: Create a new buffer with an optional initial content.

tools.name: crispy_eval
tools.description: Compile and run an inline crispy C code snippet. Returns the exit code.

code.description: crispy C source to compile and execute

tools.name: current_view
tools.description: What the user is looking at right now: the visible buffers, most recently selected first, with the AI chat surfaces excluded. Call this when the user refers to "here", "this" or "the above" without naming a buffer.

include_content.description: Also return the buffers' text (default false: the listing alone is usually enough, and get_buffer_content fetches just the one you want)

tools.name: db_columns
tools.description: Describe one table's columns on CONNECTION: name, type, nullability, default and primary-key membership, as a JSON array.  TABLE and SCHEMA must be plain unquoted identifiers.

table.description: Table or view name, e.g. users

schema.description: Schema the table lives in; omit for the default

tools.name: db_connect
tools.description: Open the saved connection named CONNECTION, so queries can run against it.  Names come from db_connections; a connection URL is not accepted.  Already-open connections are left alone.

tools.name: db_connections
tools.description: List the database connections this cmacs knows: the saved ones and which of them are currently open.  Returns a JSON array of {name, dialect, state, read_only}.  Every other db_* tool takes one of these names -- there is no way to open a database by URL.

tools.name: db_disconnect
tools.description: Close the connection named CONNECTION, releasing its database handle and dropping its cached schema.  The saved definition survives, so db_connect brings it back.

tools.name: db_execute
tools.description: Run a writing SQL statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL) on CONNECTION and return JSON {rows_affected, last_insert_rowid}.  This changes data: a connection marked read-only refuses it.

sql.description: Statement to execute, e.g. UPDATE users SET name = 'x' WHERE id = 1

tools.name: db_export
tools.description: Run SQL on CONNECTION and write the whole result to PATH in FORMAT (csv, json, org, ...), returning a status line rather than the data.  Use this instead of db_query when the result is too large to read back, or when it is wanted on disk.

tools.name: db_query
tools.description: Run a read-only SQL statement on CONNECTION and return its result as JSON {columns, rows, truncated, row_count}.  A statement that writes is refused here -- use db_execute for that.  MAX_ROWS caps the rows fetched; the reply is also cut at a fixed character budget, so prefer a narrow SELECT over 'SELECT *' on a big table.

sql.description: Read-only statement, e.g. SELECT id, name FROM users LIMIT 20

max_rows.description: Maximum rows to fetch; omit for the configured default

tools.name: db_tables
tools.description: List the tables and views on CONNECTION as a JSON array of {name, kind, schema}, optionally restricted to one SCHEMA.  Start here before writing a query against an unfamiliar database.

schema.description: Schema to restrict to; omit for the connection's default

tools.name: delete_window
tools.description: Delete (close) the currently selected window.

tools.name: describe_function
tools.description: Describe an Emacs Lisp function: arglist, docstring, and source location.

tools.name: describe_mode
tools.description: Get the current major mode and active minor modes.

tools.name: describe_variable
tools.description: Describe an Emacs Lisp variable: current value and docstring.

tools.name: edit_buffer
tools.description: Replace an exact substring in a buffer. old_string must occur exactly once unless replace_all is true. Errors if not found.

buffer.description: Buffer name

tools.name: eval
tools.description: Evaluate an Emacs Lisp expression and return the printed result. This is the universal gateway to all Emacs functionality.

tools.name: execute_command
tools.description: Execute an interactive Emacs command (M-x equivalent).

tools.name: find_file
tools.description: Open a file in Emacs (equivalent to C-x C-f / find-file).

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate an image from a text prompt and insert it into a cmacs buffer.  In an Org buffer the image is attached to the current node and previewed inline; elsewhere it is saved under cmacs-ai-image-dir.  Optional 'references' is a comma-separated list of input images to condition on, each PATH or PATH::ROLE (e.g. "logo.png::style,cat.jpg::subject") -- roles tell the model what each reference is for.  Optional 'provider' (gemini / openai / grok), 'model', 'aspect' (e.g. 16:9), 'size' (e.g. 1024x1024) and 'quality'.  Optional 'buffer' names the target buffer; the current one is used otherwise.  WARNING: this blocks the cmacs main thread for the tens of seconds generation takes.

references.description: Comma-separated PATH or PATH::ROLE reference images

buffer.description: Target buffer name

tools.name: get_buffer_content
tools.description: Read the text content of a buffer. Optionally specify start/end positions.

buffer.description: Buffer name

tools.name: get_org_content
tools.description: Parse an org-mode buffer into a structured JSON document: buffer keywords (#+TITLE etc.) plus a nested headline tree with title, level, todo, priority, tags, scheduled/deadline/closed, property drawers, and body text. match filters entries with org's agenda match syntax (e.g. "work+urgent/TODO").

buffer.description: Buffer name

match.description: org agenda match string (tags/todo/property query); empty for all entries

tools.name: gi_call
tools.description: Call a GObject Introspection function. Requires the namespace to be loaded (use gi_require first via eval).

tools.name: gi_describe
tools.description: Describe a type or function in a GI namespace.

tools.name: gi_list_functions
tools.description: List all functions in a GI namespace.

tools.name: gi_list_namespaces
tools.description: List loaded GObject Introspection namespaces.

tools.name: gnuseye_add_geofence
tools.description: Add a geofence: a circle of RADIUS_KM about LAT, LON named NAME.  Entities entering/leaving emit podomation events.

tools.name: gnuseye_brief
tools.description: Summarise the entities currently indexed on the globe (counts by kind).

tools.name: gnuseye_cii
tools.description: Compute the country-instability index from active signals; returns the ranked ISO-A3 -> score JSON.

tools.name: gnuseye_fly_to
tools.description: Fly the globe camera to LAT, LON (degrees); optional RANGE world units.

tools.name: gnuseye_forecast
tools.description: Open the 7-day point-forecast panel (Open-Meteo) for LAT, LON.

tools.name: gnuseye_list_layers
tools.description: List GNU's Eye data layers with their on/off state and group.

tools.name: gnuseye_open
tools.description: Open the GNU's Eye live planetary globe buffer.

tools.name: gnuseye_query_entities
tools.description: Query indexed entities by KIND and/or a bounding box (WEST/SOUTH/EAST/NORTH degrees); returns JSON (capped by LIMIT).

tools.name: gnuseye_refresh
tools.description: Refresh every enabled GNU's Eye layer now.

tools.name: gnuseye_toggle_layer
tools.description: Toggle a data layer on/off by NAME (e.g. satellites, aircraft, vessels, quakes, launches, fires).

tools.name: gnuseye_weather_showcase
tools.description: Light the full weather picture: tropical cyclones (tracks/cones), animated precipitation radar, cloud imagery, wind particles, METARs, and US alert zones; flies to the strongest active storm.

tools.name: goto_line
tools.description: Move point to a 1-based line number in a buffer, updating its window if one is showing.

buffer.description: Buffer name

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_add_rule
tools.description: Add, or replace by name, a broadcast rule for this session; the reply says when it cannot run.

rule.description: {name, team, when, keys: {include, exclude}, modifiers, targets, translate, mode, reset-ms, delivery, mouse, delay-ms, local}

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_add_team
tools.description: Add, or replace by name, a broadcast team for this session.

team.description: {name, slots: [{name, match, focus-key, delivery}], groups: {NAME: [slot]}}; match is a filter such as app-id = eqgame.exe

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_assign
tools.description: Put a window in a broadcast team's slot by hand.

client_id.description: The window (default: the focused one); 0 hands the slot back to its match

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_focus_slot
tools.description: Focus the window in a broadcast team's slot, viewing its tag.

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_list
tools.description: The broadcast teams and rules in force, each as YAML (JSON).

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_remove
tools.description: Remove a broadcast team or rule.

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_set
tools.description: Switch input broadcasting on, off or toggle it (a toast shows the result), or panic: off, and every key held in any window released. Or set strict one-press-one-window mode instead.

tools.name: gowl_broadcast_status
tools.description: Input broadcasting (multiboxing): whether it is on, strict mode, the toggle and panic keys, every team with the window in each slot, every rule with the reason it cannot run if any, and delivery counters (JSON). The module is opt-in.

tools.name: gowl_clipboard_copy
tools.description: Put a history entry back on the clipboard: the next paste in any window produces it. Replaces what the person has copied.

tools.name: gowl_clipboard_entry
tools.description: The path of one history entry's stored bytes (exactly what was copied, in its MIME type).

tools.name: gowl_clipboard_list
tools.description: The clipboard history, newest first: one line per entry, ID<TAB>MIME<TAB>BYTES<TAB>PREVIEW. This is everything the person copied -- passwords included -- so read it when the task needs it, not by habit. The Super+space menu keeps it private for the same reason.

tools.name: gowl_close_client
tools.description: Close the Wayland client matching a pattern.

tools.name: gowl_drain_recording
tools.description: Take everything recorded since the last drain and leave the recording running. The reply carries dropped (since the last drain) and dropped_total, so a demonstration that overflowed the ring is reported rather than passed off as complete, plus active and stop_reason.

tools.name: gowl_find_client
tools.description: Find a Wayland client by app-id or title pattern.

tools.name: gowl_focus_client
tools.description: Give keyboard focus to the Wayland client matching a pattern.

tools.name: gowl_focused_client
tools.description: Get info about the currently focused Wayland client.

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_add
tools.description: Add a hotkey (or a section of them) for this session; refused whole, with the reason, on any problem.

hotkey.description: A hotkey entry {id, key, do, context, when, mode, double, hold, ...} -- key in AutoHotkey notation (#!t, CapsLock & j, ~LButton) or gowl's (Super+Alt+t); do is a list of actions such as {shell: CMD}, {send: KEYS}, {action: spawn, arg: PROGRAM} -- or a whole section {hotkeys: [...], remaps: {...}, modes: {...}}

yaml.description: The same as one line of flow YAML

id.description: Name it, so adding again replaces it and gowl_hotkey_remove takes it back

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_fire
tools.description: Run a hotkey's actions as if it had been pressed.

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_history
tools.description: The last 64 inputs the hotkey module saw (JSON): keycode, keysym, pressed, injected, swallowed and the hotkey each fired. The first thing to look at when a hotkey does not fire.

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_list
tools.description: Every hotkey and remap in force (JSON): id, key as written and canonical, context, mode, enabled, origin, description.

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_remove
tools.description: Remove a hotkey added at run time (one from the configuration is disabled instead).

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_send
tools.description: Type keys or text into the focused window through the hotkey module.

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_set
tools.description: Switch one hotkey on or off (id + enabled), suspend every hotkey, or enter a key mode.

mode.description: A key mode; default leaves every mode

tools.name: gowl_hotkey_status
tools.description: Hotkeys (AutoHotkey for gowl): whether they are suspended, the key mode, counts of hotkeys, remaps, timers and hotstrings, the lock keys, the last hotkey fired and the last error (JSON). The module is opt-in; this loads it.

tools.name: gowl_list_clients
tools.description: List all Wayland clients (JSON array with id, title, app-id, tags, geometry).

tools.name: gowl_list_keybinds
tools.description: List all compositor keybinds.

tools.name: gowl_list_monitors
tools.description: List monitors (JSON array with name, geometry, mode, scale, layout).

tools.name: gowl_macro_list
tools.description: Every macro runnable by name, as JSON: name, kind (file, registered, custom = Elisp, ...), path, held-back.

tools.name: gowl_macro_record
tools.description: The macro recorder (Super+Alt+r). start records the person's keys, clicks, drags and scrolls; stop writes last-recording.c (and NAME.c) and replies `recorded NAME STEPS PATH'; cancel discards; status reports. Starting from here needs gowl's `input-recording' consent, because it watches the person's input; the screen is framed while it runs and password prompts are not recorded.

tools.name: gowl_macro_run
tools.description: Run a gowl macro: in-process C (crispy) or an Elisp macro that drives the compositor. Runs under gowl's fault guard and time budget; a crash or runaway loop is stopped and held back. Loads the opt-in macro module on first use.

name.description: A macro name (a file on the macro path, a registered or an Elisp macro), or a path to a .c file

tools.name: gowl_macro_status
tools.description: Running macros, held-back ones and why, the fault count, the time budget, triggers -- the macro module's status JSON.

tools.name: gowl_macro_stop
tools.description: Stop running macros.

which.description: A macro name, a run id or all (the default)

tools.name: gowl_macro_voice_match
tools.description: Run the macro a sentence names, as Super+Alt+m does with what was said: a configured phrase, a macro's name said as words ("pip corner 25" runs pip-corner 25), or every word of a name. dry_run reports what it would run (heard, normalised, macro, args) and runs nothing.

tools.name: gowl_macro_voice_status
tools.description: The voice listener's state: listening, command, time limit, last sentence heard, last error. There is no tool to start listening: the microphone is the person's to turn on.

tools.name: gowl_pick_color
tools.description: The colour of the screen at layout x, y, as "#rrggbb". The clipboard is left alone.

tools.name: gowl_recording_status
tools.description: Whether an input recording is running, its token, limits and counters, without consuming anything. Poll this to notice that a recording started, stopped, or was stopped from the keyboard.

tools.name: gowl_reload_config
tools.description: Reload the gowl compositor configuration from YAML.

tools.name: gowl_screen_text
tools.description: Read the text in a region of the screen (OCR via tesseract, the screenshot module's ocr-command), in layout coordinates as gowl_list_monitors and gowl_list_clients report them. Returns the text, "" when there is none. The clipboard is left alone unless copy is true.

language.description: tesseract languages, e.g. eng+deu (default: the screenshot module's)

copy.description: Also put the text on the clipboard (default false)

tools.name: gowl_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot and return it as a PNG image. With no arguments captures the whole desktop; mode selects desktop/window/all; client captures one matching client.

client.description: Capture the client matching this pattern

tools.name: gowl_set_client_geometry
tools.description: Move and resize the Wayland client matching a pattern in one call.

tools.name: gowl_set_layout
tools.description: Set the tiling layout: "tile", "monocle", or "float".

tools.name: gowl_set_monitor_transform
tools.description: Set the wl_output transform for a monitor (rotation/flip). transform is an integer 0-7: 0=normal, 1=90, 2=180, 3=270, 4=flipped, 5=flipped-90, 6=flipped-180, 7=flipped-270. To persist across sessions, add `transform:` under the matching output name in the YAML `monitors:` block.

tools.name: gowl_spawn
tools.description: Spawn a command in the Wayland compositor.

tools.name: gowl_start_recording
tools.description: Record real keyboard and pointer input so a human demonstration can be turned into a procedure. Returns a token for gowl_drain_recording and gowl_stop_recording. Bounded: the ring holds at most max_events (older events are dropped and counted) and the recording stops itself after max_seconds. Requires gowl's `input-recording' config key, which is separate from send_keys and off by default. While it runs the screen is framed in red and Super+Shift+Escape stops it. Capture is suppressed on the lock screen and for windows on the deny list, but gowl CANNOT see a password field inside an ordinary window -- review a trace before storing or sharing it.

max_seconds.description: Stop automatically after this many seconds (default 120, maximum 3600)

tools.name: gowl_stop_recording
tools.description: Stop the recording and take the tail, in the same shape gowl_drain_recording returns. Stopping a recording that already stopped itself still returns its remaining events exactly once.

tools.name: gowl_workspace_list
tools.description: List workspaces as plists (:id :name :tag-mask).

tools.name: gowl_workspace_switch
tools.description: Switch to the workspace with the given id.

tools.name: gsurf_back
tools.description: Navigate a gsurf buffer back.

buffer.description: gsurf buffer name; defaults to the most recent

tools.name: gsurf_click
tools.description: Click at x,y (CSS pixels from the page's top-left, as getBoundingClientRect reports) in a gsurf page with a trusted click.

buffer.description: gsurf buffer name; defaults to the most recent

tools.name: gsurf_click_element
tools.description: Click the first element matching a CSS selector in a gsurf page: it is scrolled into view, focused and clicked at its centre.  Asynchronous: returns at once; the outcome goes to the echo area.

buffer.description: gsurf buffer name; defaults to the most recent

tools.name: gsurf_current
tools.description: Return JSON for the current gsurf buffer (buffer/uri/title/progress).

tools.name: gsurf_download_cancel
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight gsurf download by id.

tools.name: gsurf_download_list
tools.description: Return a JSON array of known gsurf downloads (id/uri/dest/received/total/state).

tools.name: gsurf_eval_js
tools.description: Run JavaScript in a gsurf buffer's page (fire-and-forget).

tools.description: Return the rendered plain text of a gsurf-lite buffer (newest, or the named one).  Reads a JS-rendered or logged-in page as clean text after gsurf_lite_open.
